So I'm venting and it's cathartic in a way for me. I apologize if this isn't the place for it. But /v/offmychest just doesn't seem like I'll get any constructive criticism.

But it's been incredibly hard for 2 years now. My son, who is amazing is turning 3 in September. He still doesn't speak more than 10 words. He doesn't jump up and down. He can't eat with a fork and doesn't eat only 15-20 different types of food total, all of which fit within the snack/fast-food realm. He fills and dumps and crashes toys together.

And I love him to death in spite of his shortcomings.

He's an amazingly bright kid. You can see in his mind that he KNOWS what to do. He knows what to say. I watch him climb a small rock wall and I see him look at the wall and figure out his 'lines' to the top. I see him look at a puzzle and know how the pieces interact and complete. I watch as he looks at an educational toy and is more interested in figuring out how it works than to play with it. He knows where he placed a toy 2 days later after he set it down.

But when I take him out of the house, I lose all frame of reference of how bright and special he is.

I see a child 2 years younger than him speaking better and more words than him. Children his age asking me questions and exploring the world. And it breaks my heart to know how frustrated my son gets at not being able to tell me what's wrong when he's frustrated. I make excuses for him to other people and sometimes have to explain to little kids that he's just growing up at his own pace.

He's been in Developmental intervention since he was 1. Physical therapy, Occupational therapy, Speech Therapy and now a Nutritionist as well. We are scheduled to have him tested for Autism too in another month but I'm not sure what level of spectrum he would fall on due to his awareness of surroundings and his social desire to interact with people.

I put on a brave face for my wife who is unshaken by this and relates to the world much differently but inside there are days where I just cannot take it and just put on a movie for him as I try to ignore the present. My wife is a very successful accountant so she is gone during the day, and I do personal training, but with everything happening with my son, I've cut down my clientele base quite a bit and work with a select few. So I'm the front line of parenting which makes it a little harder for me than for her.

 

I guess my question to all the parents out there is how do I keep up feeling positive when sometimes it just seems as if there is no end in sight to the struggles we as a family currently face? I had so many exciting things I wanted to do with my son pre-birth and now I just want to be able to talk to him and let him know that he is loved. I wanted to show him the world and I'm just a little frustrated that it may never happen.

Someone toss me a line of hope here. I'm starting to drown in a little self-pity/depression about things.
Anyone have advice on how not to get frustrated at things out of your control?

It's hard for me to think of a response that doesn't sound trite, but remember that things will work out, even when it seems they wont.

I would suggest that taking some time to decompress may be required. Perhaps hire a babysitter, or have your wife look after your son while you take a half day to enjoy some relaxing adult only activities (beer, fishing, fight club, or whatever floats your boat). If you are running out of patience, then the best thing for everyone is for you to take some time to get it back.

I see this a lot in my line of work, where not enough time is taken to decompress after stressful situations. It will build and build, day after day until It makes even the smallest things more difficult.

I would also stop worrying about how he compares to other children, I see plenty of people that are 20 years younger than me excel in areas that i still can't manage very well. Instead, you can focus on how much he has learned or changed. As the primary care giver, it may take a little more of an effort to see it, since changes may be gradual, but i'll bet it's there.

I think it's just getting out of the house that makes it most difficult and i remind myself that 'This too shall pass".

I figure in 10-20 years this will be a memory, but to compare it to my exercise, while you're right in the middle of your lift, it feels as if you're taking on the world.

Sometimes I just need to vent though and unfortunately we don't know anyone in similar situations lol. Trying to find that 'Dads group with kids with slightly special needs, but not so far as to need full interventions" is such a niche group.

Thank you though for your kind words. A friend of mine said that I need to just focus on the positives and sometimes it just is a little difficult to do so as we go into parenting with expectations and when those are shot down, you try to find new expectations to fit your child. With me it's just a matter of still trying to re-frame my son's progression into manageable goals that I can enjoy when he achieves them.

Have you taken him to see a specialist? It's possible that maybe there is just a minor thing that can be easily treated by physical therapy, trainings, etc. I say this as a mom of a child born 9 weeks premature. She is constantly getting checked to make sure she can hit milestones. If it looks like there are possible issues she gets checked by a specialist. Sometimes the "solution" is something as simple as tweaking a playtime routine to make her use a different set of muscles, Etc. There is no shame in seeking a medical opinion.

He has seen every specialist short of a psychologist. We've been doing everything from physical therapy to speech to behavioral.

Autism is getting tested next month I believe through his pediatrician, and he's in early developmental pre school at the moment for 2 hours a day.

We play the hand we're dealt, but sometimes it's difficult.

I'm sure that we'll figure out ways to communicate and relate to each other, but you never think that your child will be the one with issues. Especially with two healthy adults.

Oh ok, if it is autism remember there has been so much improvement in behavior therapy that it's not as unmanageable of a diagnosis as it use to be. I am out of bounds to give you advice. just dig deep in yourself and love for your child and take it moment by moment. When I was in NICU I would sometimes just have to make it for five more minutes, I couldn't think about the whole day, let alone the two months we were there. I noticed the doctors response for every parent who asked how long they would stay was "three weeks". If parents were told two months they would get overwhelmed, but three weeks? You can keep it up for three weeks, then another. I use that when I get overwhelmed. "Okay, we made it through breakfast, how will I make it for the next two hours (or half hour, or five minutes). Good luck. You will make it through, you have too. It's what parents do!

• Eyes at 12 (feet at 11, as you do currently).

  • Dig branches off the main shaft every 4th block, leaving 3 blocks between each branch. I generally mine each branch between 100 and 150m, depends on how I'm feeling that day. If you're really anal, you can go 160m for each branch to cover 10 chunks worth of distance.

  • This will reveal almost every diamond cluster between layers 10-13. The only ones you miss will be the 1x1 and 1x2 clusters that might spawn in between the branches of your mine.

Mining Engineer here: I do a standard room-n-pillar setup.

When creating tunnels, I usually get some TNT (or Industrial TNT preferably in a mod), and dig two in, place TNT, ignite TNT, place block in front. It blasts out a 3x3x3 in standard rock.

That branch mining method would work well with creating main tunnels to expand operations and increase access and navigation.

Here’s an important point many people fail to realize: given the size of the Minecraft world, the time you spend mining is far more valuable than actually getting every single diamond vein. Knowing this, you will want to avoid any chance of redundant tunnels searching the same chunk for diamonds you’ve already found. You don’t want to walk too far between your mine’s branches either, so spacing them too widely is no go.

I branch mine. I figure around ~5 blocks between branches is good, but not on the same level. When I start a mine, I just stay on one level (feet at y=11), with a branch every 10 blocks. My main tunnel is usually 2×2, but it’s kinda personal preference. I make my branches 100 long—the round number makes it easy to watch my coords to know when the end is coming. I also like to cap each tunnel with a fence gate to stop any mobs from caves wandering into the main corridor. If I find I start to have to walk too far to get to the next unfinished tunnel, I’ll start to do tunnels between and 2 block up. I just plop a single ladder at eye level for each one in the main tunnel.

I prefer jack-o-lanterns in the floor for lighting, and I like to place them frequently enough so no mobs spawn. Depending on how you play, glowstone may eventually be even cheaper (and you can place them over air). In either case, they’re water proof and you won’t accidentally knock them off the wall.

cobblestone slabs are great for bridging gaps and lava.

When I have a beacon and enough iron, I just do the haste II efficiency V diamond pickaxe thing and clear out big swathes. I like my efficiency V pickaxe to have silk touch so I get mountains of smooth stone, and don’t accidentally mine any ores with a non-fortune pickaxe.

To be maximally time efficient, branch mine and put a branch every 6 to 7 blocks. Your main tunnel will look something like: http://www.minecraft101.net/reference/images/branch-mine-hallway.jpg

I usually do every 5, on the 5. For example, x=100, x=105, x=110. That's because I run my branches out about 150 to 200 blocks, turn 5 blocks, and mine back. That means I always hit some cave or something and it's easier to figure out where to make the return branch.

The hardest thing about this is you have to get over the fact that you WILL miss some diamonds. The way to get over this is to remember that within 2000 blocks of you, there are more diamonds than you can reasonably use. It doesn't matter if you miss some of them. You want to find more of the large clusters per unit time spent mining and spreading your branches out will let you do that.

Other little tips:

  • I also usually mine at y=12 so I'm above most of the lava.
  • Put a torch every 10 tiles. You can mine 5 ahead of you, so the rhythm is mine 5, walk to wall, mine 5, set torch. Repeat. This will prevent mobs from spawning.
  • If you are using the mine out, turn, mine back method, put torches on the walls to indicate the direction you need to turn. I'm ADD and always forget.
  • when you are done with a branch, dig out the floor two deep or put in a fence. This will prevent mobs from sneaking up on you.
